claims.explanation: Nabumetone is a non-acidic prodrug NSAID whose active metabolite inhibits COX-1/COX-2, but its selective antiproliferative pattern across cancer lines is not explained by COX expression alone; the strongest signal is that lines with intact p53 signaling and low mesenchymal/EMT or low NF-kB/COX-2 inflammatory tone are more sensitive, while lines with RAS/RAF-driven MAPK activation, PTEN loss/PI3K activation, or mesenchymal phenotype are relatively protected. The virtual-cell response showing MAPK/NF-kB pathway transcripts and similarity to ibuprofen supports a COX/prostaglandin- and inflammation-linked mechanism, with TP53 status and lineage context modulating the downstream apoptotic response.

features.basis: Most resistant lines retain TP53 mutations or wild-type-like p53 signaling, whereas sensitive lines often have TP53 mutations but still show apoptotic competence; p53 loss may blunt nabumetone-induced
BRAF-mutant melanoma and colorectal lines (K029AX, SNUC5, HEC265) are less consistently killed, suggesting MAPK-driven resistance
KRAS-mutant lines (OV7, CL11, SNU410, T3M4, GSU) are enriched among resistant lines, consistent with RAS-MAPK-mediated survival
PTEN-mutant lines (786O, FTC133, ZR751, UACC62, KALS1) appear in both groups but PTEN loss/PI3K activation may reduce dependence on COX-mediated apoptosis
EGFR-mutant NSCLC lines (HCC4006, NCIH1650, KYSE270) are among the most killed, suggesting EGFR-driven dependency enhances nabumetone sensitivity
CDKN2A loss is common in sensitive lines (K029AX, SNU1214, MHHES1, IPC298), possibly reflecting cell-cycle deregulation that increases drug sensitivity
High COX-2 (PTGS2) expression may sequester nabumetone's active metabolite and reduce free drug available to inhibit pro-apoptotic prostaglandin synthesis
COX-1 expression in platelets/endothelium may buffer the drug's effect and protect lines with high constitutive COX-1
NF1-mutant lines (FTC133, KALS1, BICR6, S117) are enriched in the resistant set, consistent with RAS pathway activation
SMARCA4-mutant lines (OV7, KYSE270) are among the most killed, suggesting chromatin-remodeling defects increase sensitivity
NOTCH1-mutant lines (KYSE270) are sensitive, and virtual-cell data show NOTCH1 upregulation, linking Notch signaling to nabumetone response
ARID1A-mutant lines (SNUC5, HEC265, KU1919) appear in both groups but ARID1A loss may sensitize to COX inhibition via altered inflammatory signaling
